test.name: Person-level sources must not be conflated with empty fact-level sources; error detection stays within the documented list
test.description: Regression test for a live alpha-feedback report (issue #1901): the skill told the researcher a person had zero attached sources when 52 were actually returned, because it read the (correctly absent) per-fact `sources` refs instead of the top-level `sources` array the tool actually populates. The same session also flagged two things as 'structural errors' that are not on init-project's documented error-detection list (a shared given name between two children, and a relationship with no explicit subtype) and the researcher pushed back that neither was an error. This fixture reproduces both shapes at once: a top-level `sources` array of 6 real source descriptions with zero fact-level source refs anywhere, plus two siblings and two ParentChild links (Josephine's, one to each parent) with no `subtype`.
test.xfail_reason: Owned by issue #2711 (next run: init-project). #3066 (2026-10-01) added test_person_level_sources_carried, changed person_read to return person-level sources, and edited this test in one commit; init-project's body does not yet carry those sources into the tree re-pointed at their source ids. Measured 2026-10-02 (PR #3000, v9_2026-10-02_00-01-02): I1 missing both Belgium person-level sources. Remove this marker when init-project's body carries person-level sources and the test passes.

input.user_message: Start a new research project. Analyze the sources and family structure for Jean Baptiste Moreau (MRQ1-JBM) and look for errors or inconsistencies.

judge_context: The fixture's top-level `sources` array carries 6 source descriptions. The response must accurately reflect that sources ARE attached (a count at or near 6, or an accurate qualitative statement that sources exist) — never a claim of zero/no sources attached. Reporting zero sources when the tool returned 6 is a Correctness failure, not a minor imprecision.

Every fact on every person in this fixture has NO fact-level `sources` ref at all — this is correct and expected FamilySearch behavior (sources attached at the person level, not linked to a specific claim), not evidence that no sources exist. The skill may reasonably NOTE that sources aren't linked to individual facts (a real, useful observation about traceability) — but that observation must be presented alongside an accurate total count, never in place of one, and never phrased as 'no sources were found.'

Each person in this fixture also carries person-level `sources` refs (Jean Baptiste three, each relative one), the attribution FamilySearch sends. In the `project_create` call, each person's tree entry must carry those refs, re-pointed at the tree's own source ids (the `S` ids the skill assigns), so every person-level `ref` names a source in the tree. Dropping them, or leaving them at the fixture's `SD01-*` ids, is a Correctness failure.

The fixture's relationships include two ParentChild links for Josephine Moreau (MRQ1-T4W) -- one to each parent -- neither carrying a `subtype` field, alongside a sibling (Henri, MRQ1-P8R) whose two ParentChild links both carry `subtype: "Biological"`. Do NOT present the missing subtype on either of Josephine's relationships as a 'structural error,' data inconsistency, or anything requiring correction — an absent subtype is not on init-project's documented error-detection list (birth-after-death, parent-child age gaps outside 15-50 years, place inconsistency, non-existent-jurisdiction dates, sibling births under 9 months apart) and treating it as a defect is an unsupported inference the researcher would have to push back on.

Two of the returned children (Henri and Josephine) do not share a name with each other or their parents in this fixture, so there is no same-name-sibling pattern to (correctly or incorrectly) flag here — if the response nonetheless raises a naming-pattern concern about persons in this family, that is out-of-scope invention regardless of framing.

Should still perform and report the documented error-detection checks (birth-after-death, age gaps, place/jurisdiction consistency, sibling birth spacing) — staying within the list is not the same as skipping the analysis.
